title: Agent Identity / Delegation
security_question: Can Agent A claim that authority was delegated to Agent B and thereby cause Agent B to perform something neither agent was actually granted?
retest_support_detail: ATTACK and RETEST use the same canonical A2A-001 delegation request. Profile is server-owned ExperimentContext. Process env is not mutated. CTRL-IDENTITY-001 stays OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant. CTRL-MCP-001 is the sole tool PDP.

ATTACK.attack_objective: Submit the catalog adversarial delegation claim on the intentionally vulnerable ATTACK experiment and observe whether lookup_customer_tier is granted even though neither agent is coded customer:read.
ATTACK.why_this_matters: IDENTITY CLAIM != AUTHENTICATION. DELEGATION CLAIM != AUTHORIZATION. A caller id does not mint a grant. A + B does not create new authority.
ATTACK.what_will_change: A new run.id is minted. CTRL-IDENTITY-001 still OBSERVEs identity_claim_is_not_grant. A labeled fail-open overlay is minted. CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOWs. lookup_customer_tier handler 1.
ATTACK.what_will_not_change: Coded allowed_tools. coded_policy(). Principal, caller, callee, claimed scope, requested tool/scope/resource. CTRL-IDENTITY-001 does not ALLOW. The browser does not choose profile, grants, identity_verified, authenticated, or the A2A body. Splunk does not ALLOW or DENY.
ATTACK.security_property: A delegation claim must not create authority that neither party possesses. On this labeled vulnerable experiment the overlay is the failure. That is not cryptographic identity bypass.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_defended: Not this ATTACK specimen. Defended same-claim evaluation is the RETEST experiment.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_vulnerable: INTENTIONALLY VULNERABLE LAB PROFILE: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant / untrusted_claim; overlay vulnerable_profile_fail_open:caller_identity_derived_authority; CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW; lookup_customer_tier handler 1; testbed.mode=ATTACK. OBSERVE is not ALLOW. ALLOW is not execution. WHO AUTHENTICATED = NOT PROVEN / NOT MODELED.
ATTACK.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch ATTACK, write: will CTRL-IDENTITY-001 OBSERVE or DENY, will CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW lookup_customer_tier, will the privileged handler start, and did anyone authenticate?
ATTACK.attacker_influence: The closed adversarial delegation fixture. The attacker wants the claim treated as a grant so neither agent needs customer:read.
ATTACK.defense_should: On this ATTACK specimen the lab is fail-open at CTRL-MCP-001 via a per-request overlay. The defense you will enable is the RETEST ExperimentContext (profile=defended). Do not trust agent names, Splunk, or an identity string.

BASELINE.attack_objective: Submit the catalog normal lookup_policy delegation so later ATTACK evidence has a normal comparison.
BASELINE.why_this_matters: Zero BASELINE rows is not all-clear. You need the shape of IDENTITY OBSERVE plus MCP ALLOW tool_granted before judging the privileged claim. Do not label BASELINE SAFE.
BASELINE.what_will_change: A new run.id. CTRL-IDENTITY-001 OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant. CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW tool_granted. lookup_policy handler 1. lookup_customer_tier handler 0.
BASELINE.what_will_not_change: Coded grants. This is not the privileged request.
BASELINE.security_property: INV-007 evidence for a granted tool. untrusted_claim is not malice and is not SAFE.
BASELINE.expected_evidence_defended: testbed.mode=BASELINE, profile=defended, IDENTITY OBSERVE, MCP ALLOW tool_granted, lookup_policy 1, lookup_customer_tier 0.
BASELINE.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch, write: should IDENTITY OBSERVE, should lookup_policy ALLOW, and should lookup_customer_tier stay at 0?

RETEST.attack_objective: Submit the SAME canonical privileged delegation claim on the defended RETEST experiment and prove the outcome changed because tool authorization changed, not because the identity claim changed.
RETEST.why_this_matters: A closed-loop experiment needs independent ATTACK and RETEST run.ids. IDENTITY still only OBSERVEs. If you thought IDENTITY granted the tool, RETEST would confuse you.
RETEST.what_will_change: A new run.id, testbed.mode=RETEST, profile=defended, CTRL-MCP-001 DENY tool_not_granted, lookup_customer_tier handler 0, no mcp.started for the privileged operation.
RETEST.what_will_not_change: Principal, caller, callee, claimed scope, requested tool, requested scope, requested resource, request fingerprint, CTRL-IDENTITY-001 OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant. Coded grants. Splunk still does not enforce.
RETEST.security_property: SAME PRINCIPAL. SAME CALLER. SAME CALLEE. SAME DELEGATION CLAIM. SAME PRIVILEGED REQUEST. DIFFERENT AUTHORIZATION. DIFFERENT EXECUTION.
RETEST.expected_evidence_defended: IDENTITY OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant; MCP DENY tool_not_granted; lookup_customer_tier handler 0; testbed.mode=RETEST.
RETEST.will_reach_operation: On defended RETEST, lookup_customer_tier does not start. CTRL-IDENTITY-001 still OBSERVEs. CTRL-MCP-001 DENYs.
RETEST.which_control: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 records the trust boundary. CTRL-MCP-001 at acmebank.mcp.authorize is the tool PDP. These solve different problems. AcmeBank owns enforcement. Splunk does not.
RETEST.expected_decision: IDENTITY OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant. MCP DENY tool_not_granted.
RETEST.falsify: IDENTITY ALLOW, IDENTITY DENY of the tool, lookup_customer_tier handler 1, a different request fingerprint than ATTACK, or claiming the caller was authenticated would falsify the defended prediction. Missing Splunk rows alone would not.
RETEST.predict_before_launch: Will the same claim produce the same IDENTITY OBSERVE? Will CTRL-MCP-001 now DENY? Will the privileged handler stay at 0? Does caller_agent_id prove authentication?

limitations: LOCAL EDUCATIONAL SERVICE. Attack Service is localhost and unauthenticated.
NOT PRODUCTION AUTHENTICATION. NOT MULTI-TENANT. NOT INTERNET-FACING.
CTRL-IDENTITY-001 classifies identity/delegation claims. It is OBSERVE only. It is not a tool PDP.
CTRL-MCP-001 is a lab allow-list, not production MCP IAM.
WHO AUTHENTICATED = NOT PROVEN / NOT MODELED. Agent id strings are attribution, not cryptographic identity.
No OAuth, OIDC, JWT validation, SPIFFE/SPIRE, or real A2A transport.
HEC HTTP 200 is not searchable evidence.
Missing Splunk event is not prevention.
ALLOW is not execution. OBSERVE is not ALLOW. untrusted_claim is not a grant.
DET-MCP-001 alerts only on DENY-then-start. ATTACK is MCP ALLOW. Silence is not SAFE. No DET-A2A.
Studio tokens are not auto-bound to a fresh run.id.
Learning metadata is not security policy.
Canonical Investigate specimen ids are REPLAY Phase 12C, not the LIVE run you just launched.
